sides.text: AWS shared responsibility model
AWS secures the cloud (hardware, facilities, managed-service software). You secure what you put in it (data, IAM, OS patching on EC2, security groups)

more.text: Responsibility shifts toward AWS for managed services such as RDS and Lambda.

sides.text: AWS Regions and Availability Zones
A Region is a geographic area with multiple isolated AZs; an AZ is one or more data centers

more.text: Design across at least two AZs. Data stays in a Region unless you move it.

sides.text: IAM user, group, role, policy
User: long-term identity. Group: set of users. Role: assumable identity with temporary credentials. Policy: JSON permissions document

more.text: Prefer roles over long-term access keys.

sides.text: Root user best practices
Enable MFA, delete or never create access keys, use only for tasks that require it, lock away credentials

more.text: Create admin IAM users or use IAM Identity Center for daily work.

sides.text: IAM policy evaluation logic
Default deny. An explicit Deny always wins. Otherwise an Allow is needed

more.text: Organization SCPs and permission boundaries only limit; they never grant.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A user has no policy mentioning DynamoDB. Can they call dynamodb:ListTables?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: No

more.text: Everything is denied by default

sides.text: Identity-based vs resource-based policies
Identity-based attach to users, groups, or roles. Resource-based attach to the resource (S3 bucket, SQS queue, KMS key) and name a principal

more.text: Cross-account access can use a resource policy alone for some services.

sides.text: Least privilege
Grant only the permissions needed; start narrow and widen with evidence

more.text: IAM Access Analyzer and last-accessed data show unused permissions.

sides.text: IAM roles for services
EC2 instance profiles and Lambda execution roles deliver temporary credentials to code

more.text: Never embed access keys in AMIs or code.

sides.text: AWS STS and AssumeRole
Security Token Service issues temporary credentials for roles

more.text: Cross-account: the trusted account's principal calls AssumeRole on a role in the target account.

sides.text: Permissions boundary
An IAM policy that sets the maximum permissions a user or role can have

more.text: Effective permissions are the intersection of identity policy and boundary.

sides.text: MFA

Adds a second factor:
virtual authenticator
FIDO2 security key
hardware TOTP

more.text: Can be required in policy with the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition.

sides.text: Password policy and key rotation

Set password rules in IAM
rotate access keys
remove unused credentials

more.text: The credential report lists key age and MFA status.

sides.text: IAM policy condition keys
Restrict by source IP, VPC endpoint, time, MFA, tags, or organization ID

more.text: aws:SourceIp, aws:SourceVpce, aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:RequestedRegion.

sides.text: Attribute-based access control (ABAC)
Allow by matching tags on principals and resources

more.text: Scales better than per-resource policies.

sides.text: AWS Organizations
Central management of many accounts with consolidated billing and policies

more.text: Organizational units (OUs) group accounts for policy inheritance.

sides.text: Service control policies (SCPs)
Guardrails that cap the maximum permissions in member accounts

more.text: They do not grant permissions and do not apply to the management account.

sides.text: AWS Control Tower
Sets up a multi-account landing zone with guardrails and automated account provisioning

more.text: Built on Organizations, Config, and Service Catalog.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A company wants a governed multi-account environment with guardrails quickly

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: AWS Control Tower

more.text: It builds on Organizations to create a landing zone

sides.text: IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO)
Single sign-on across accounts and applications using a built-in directory or an external IdP

more.text: Permission sets map users and groups to accounts.

sides.text: Federation

Let corporate identities access AWS without IAM users:
SAML 2.0
OIDC
Identity Center

more.text: Users receive temporary role credentials.

sides.text: Amazon Cognito user pools
User directory for app sign-up and sign-in that issues JWT tokens

more.text: Supports social and SAML IdPs and MFA.

sides.text: Amazon Cognito identity pools
Exchange tokens for temporary AWS credentials to access AWS services directly

more.text: Used with user pools or external IdPs.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A mobile app must upload directly to S3 using temporary credentials. Which?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: A Cognito identity pool

more.text: User pools authenticate; identity pools provide AWS credentials

sides.text: AWS Directory Service
Managed Microsoft AD for a full AD in AWS, AD Connector to proxy on-premises AD, Simple AD for basic needs

more.text: Use when Windows workloads need domain services.

sides.text: Cross-account access pattern
Create a role in the resource account that trusts the other account, then assume it

more.text: Avoids sharing access keys.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Account A's users must access an S3 bucket in account B without sharing keys

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Create a role in B trusting A, grant S3 access, and have A's users assume it

more.text: Or add a bucket policy naming A's principals

sides.text: Resource Access Manager (RAM)
Share resources (subnets, Transit Gateway, license configs) across accounts without copying
Security groups

Stateful, instance-level firewall
allow rules only
all outbound allowed by default

more.text: Return traffic is automatic. Reference other security groups as sources.

sides.text: Network ACLs
Stateless, subnet-level, numbered allow and deny rules evaluated in order

more.text: Allow return ephemeral ports (1024–65535) explicitly.

sides.text: Security group vs NACL
SG: stateful, instance, allow only. NACL: stateless, subnet, allow and deny

more.text: NACLs can block a specific IP; security groups cannot deny.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: You must block a single abusive IP address. Which control?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: A network ACL deny rule

more.text: Security groups only allow

sides.text: Public and private subnets
A public subnet routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway. A private subnet has no such route

more.text: Put web tiers in public (or behind a load balancer) and data tiers in private subnets.

sides.text: Internet gateway and NAT gateway
IGW gives two-way internet access to public IPs. A NAT gateway lets private instances initiate outbound traffic only

more.text: The NAT gateway lives in a public subnet and is AZ-scoped; use one per AZ for resilience.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Private instances need to download patches. What must be added?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: A NAT gateway in a public subnet plus a private route table entry to it

more.text: 0.0.0.0/0 in the private route table points to the NAT gateway

sides.text: Egress-only internet gateway
Outbound-only internet access for IPv6 from a VPC
VPC endpoints
Gateway endpoints (S3, DynamoDB) add a route and are free. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) create ENIs for most other services

more.text: Keeps traffic off the public internet.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: EC2 in a private subnet must reach S3 without internet access and at no extra charge. Choose?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: A gateway VPC endpoint for S3

more.text: Gateway endpoints are free and route by prefix list

sides.text: AWS PrivateLink
Expose a service privately to other VPCs through an endpoint, with no peering or internet

more.text: Traffic flows only toward the service.

sides.text: AWS WAF
Layer 7 web application firewall on CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, and AppSync

more.text: Blocks SQL injection, XSS, bad IPs, and rate floods.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A web app behind an ALB suffers SQL injection attempts. Add what?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: AWS WAF with managed SQL injection rules

more.text: WAF inspects HTTP at Layer 7

sides.text: AWS Shield
Standard: free, automatic Layer 3/4 DDoS protection. Advanced: paid, extra detection, DDoS response team, cost protection

more.text: Pair with CloudFront and Route 53 for resilience.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: DDoS protection with cost protection and a response team. Which?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Shield Advanced

more.text: Standard is automatic and free

sides.text: AWS Firewall Manager and Network Firewall
Firewall Manager centrally applies WAF and security group rules across accounts. Network Firewall is a managed VPC-level stateful firewall with IPS
Amazon GuardDuty
Threat detection from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs using ML

more.text: Finds crypto-mining, credential exfiltration, and unusual API calls.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Detect a compromised instance contacting a known malicious IP. Which?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Amazon GuardDuty

more.text: It analyzes DNS, flow, and CloudTrail logs

sides.text: Amazon Macie
Discovers and classifies sensitive data such as PII in S3

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Find PII across hundreds of S3 buckets. Which service?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Amazon Macie

more.text: It classifies sensitive data automatically

sides.text: Amazon Inspector
Automated vulnerability scanning of EC2, container images in ECR, and Lambda
AWS Secrets Manager
Stores and automatically rotates secrets (database credentials, API keys)

more.text: Use SSM Parameter Store for cheaper static configuration without automatic rotation.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: An application needs a database password that rotates every 30 days. Which service?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: AWS Secrets Manager

more.text: It rotates secrets with Lambda; Parameter Store lacks automatic rotation

sides.text: Application secrets rule
Never hard-code credentials; fetch from Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, or use IAM roles
AWS Security Hub
Aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and partners; checks standards such as CIS
Amazon Detective
Investigates security findings using graph analysis of logs
Securing connections to AWS
Site-to-Site VPN is encrypted over the internet. Direct Connect is private but not encrypted by default

more.text: Combine Direct Connect with a VPN for encrypted private connectivity.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Private, consistent bandwidth to AWS but traffic must also be encrypted. How?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: Direct Connect with a Site-to-Site VPN over it

more.text: DX alone is not encrypted

sides.text: AWS Client VPN
Managed OpenVPN-based VPN for remote users to reach VPC and on-premises resources
Common external threats

DDoS
SQL injection
XSS
brute force
credential stuffing
bots

more.text: Layered defense: CloudFront, WAF, Shield, security groups, private subnets.

sides.text: AWS service endpoints
Public regional endpoints, FIPS endpoints, and VPC interface endpoints

more.text: Choose private endpoints to avoid internet exposure.

sides.text: Encryption at rest
Encrypt EBS, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS with KMS keys

more.text: Enabled by default for S3 (SSE-S3) and DynamoDB.

sides.text: AWS KMS
Managed service to create and control encryption keys with audit in CloudTrail

more.text: Key policies are the primary access control; grants delegate access.

sides.text: KMS key types
AWS owned keys, AWS managed keys (aws/service), customer managed keys

more.text: Customer managed keys give control over policy, rotation, and deletion.

sides.text: Envelope encryption
A data key encrypts the data; a KMS key encrypts the data key

more.text: Efficient for large data; only the small data key goes through KMS.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Why not encrypt a 5 GB file directly with KMS?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: KMS encrypts only up to 4 KB per call; use a data key

more.text: Generate a data key, encrypt the file locally, store the encrypted data key with it

sides.text: KMS key rotation
Customer managed keys can rotate automatically each year (optional); AWS managed keys rotate automatically

more.text: Rotation changes backing key material, not the key ID.

sides.text: Multi-Region keys
Related KMS keys in different Regions that share key material for cross-Region decryption
AWS CloudHSM
Dedicated single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware security modules that you control

more.text: Use when compliance demands customer-managed HSMs.

sides.text: S3 server-side encryption
SSE-S3 (S3-managed keys), SSE-KMS (KMS keys, audit), SSE-C (customer-provided keys), plus client-side encryption

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Auditors need to see every use of the encryption key. Which option?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: SSE-KMS

more.text: Each use is logged in CloudTrail

sides.text: Encryption in transit
TLS everywhere; AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) issues and renews public certificates for integrated services

more.text: ACM certs attach to ELB, CloudFront, and API Gateway. They cannot be exported (public certs).

sides.text: S3 security controls
Block Public Access, bucket policies, ACLs (disabled by default), Object Lock, versioning, MFA Delete

more.text: Object Lock supports WORM retention for compliance.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Prevent anyone from deleting or overwriting objects for 7 years for compliance

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode

more.text: WORM retention that even root cannot shorten

sides.text: S3 Block Public Access
Account and bucket settings that override public ACLs and policies
S3 Access Points and presigned URLs
Access points give per-application policies. Presigned URLs give temporary object access
Data backup and replication
AWS Backup centralizes backup policies. S3 Cross-Region Replication copies objects. RDS snapshots and cross-Region copies protect databases
AWS Backup
Policy-based backups across EC2, EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx; supports Vault Lock for immutability and cross-account copy
Data retention and lifecycle
S3 lifecycle rules, backup retention periods, and Object Lock define how long data persists
AWS CloudTrail
Records API calls and account activity for audit

more.text: Enable organization trails to all Regions; deliver to S3 with log file validation.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Who deleted this security group yesterday?

sides.head: Answer
sides.text: CloudTrail event history

more.text: It records API calls with caller identity and time

sides.text: AWS Config
Records resource configuration changes and evaluates compliance rules

more.text: Use for continuous compliance and drift tracking.

sides.text: AWS Artifact
On-demand access to AWS compliance reports and agreements (SOC, PCI, ISO)
Data classification and governance
Tag data by sensitivity; use Macie, Lake Formation permissions, and IAM to control access
Compliance alignment

HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, FedRAMP:
choose eligible services
encryption
logging
Region placement

more.text: AWS GovCloud isolates US government workloads.

sides.text: VPC Flow Logs
Capture IP traffic metadata for ENIs, subnets, or VPCs to CloudWatch Logs or S3

more.text: Does not capture packet payloads.

sides.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs and alarms
Centralize logs and metrics; alarms trigger actions or notifications

Over HTTP, not HTTPS

sides.code:
Allow  s3:GetObject  on reports/*
Deny   s3:*  on *
       when SecureTransport = false

sides.text: Denied
sides.head: Answer

more.text:
The Allow covers GetObject on reports/*
The Deny applies when aws:SecureTransport is false
Explicit deny wins

sides.text:
PutObject on reports/q1.csv
Over HTTPS
sides.head: Interpret
sides.code:
Allow  s3:GetObject  on reports/*
Deny   s3:*  on *
       when SecureTransport = false

sides.text: Denied (no Allow)
sides.head: Answer

more.text: Only GetObject is allowed; everything else is denied by default

sides.text:
GetObject on reports/q1.csv
Over HTTPS
sides.head: Interpret
sides.code:
Allow  s3:GetObject  on reports/*
Deny   s3:*  on *
       when SecureTransport = false

sides.text: Allowed
sides.head: Answer

more.text: Allow matches; the Deny condition is false
